## Excursions to Floreana Island from Santa Cruz

[Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) is one of the inhabited islands of the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Volcanic coastlines, beaches and birdwatching sites share the island with stories of pirates, whalers and early settlers. A visit is quite different from excursions around the more populous [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/): Floreana reveals how human history and wildlife coexist on a remote island.

Our selection includes a separate [“Floreana Island from Santa Cruz” excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/floreana-island-tour-from-santa-cruz/). The trip departs from Puerto Ayora and lasts **6 hours**, combining historical stories with natural experiences.

## The Ada Tours excursion itinerary

The departure point is [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) on Santa Cruz. The excursion includes an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, a transfer and lunch. Travelers head to Floreana, learn about the island's history and observe seabirds and other wildlife in their natural habitat. Species mentioned in the description include blue-footed boobies, sea turtles and whitetip reef sharks.

**The excursion costs $366.** National park admission, the transit card, insurance and personal expenses are listed separately. The precise natural stops and visiting order may change; do not assume every famous part of Floreana is guaranteed to be included.

## What makes Floreana Island notable?

At Post Office Bay, the story of the wooden postal barrel dates back to the late eighteenth century, when sailors used it to exchange letters. Travelers could take a letter if they were headed toward its destination and deliver it to the recipient. This custom makes the bay one of the Galápagos' unusual attractions, where human history is the central story.

[Punta Cormorant](/ecuador/place/punta-cormorant/) is known for two contrasting beaches: one with greenish sand associated with the mineral olivine, and the other with pale sand made from crushed coral particles. A nearby lagoon offers opportunities to observe flamingos. These places are described in materials published by Galápagos Conservancy. However, they **are not listed as mandatory stops on Ada Tours' six-hour excursion**; access depends on the specific authorized route.

## How this trip differs from diving

We also offer [“Galápagos: a diving day with 2 dives”](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/). Floreana is one of the possible dive sites on the dive center's weekly schedule, with a separate marine itinerary and requirements for participants.

| Purpose of the trip | Format |
|---|---|
| Exploring Floreana | Island excursion |
| History of the settlers | Walk and guided storytelling |
| Wildlife near the shore | Nature watching |
| Underwater life | Separate diving day |

The standard Floreana excursion **does not automatically include two scuba dives**. If your main aim is to see marine animals underwater with scuba equipment, choose the diving program and consider your experience and possible changes to the marine schedule.

## Planning your visit and conservation rules

The Galápagos Islands are a UNESCO World Heritage site. Access to particular natural areas is regulated by the national park. Stay on designated routes, follow your guide's instructions, do not feed birds or sea lions, and keep your distance from wildlife.

For the sea crossing, bring sun protection, a light waterproof jacket and comfortable non-slip footwear. Travelers prone to seasickness should assess the conditions of the marine portion of the excursion beforehand.

## Frequently asked questions about the Floreana excursion

### How long is the trip from Santa Cruz?

Our excursion lasts **6 hours**.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch is included along with the transfer and services of an English- or Spanish-speaking guide.

### Can visitors see the famous postal barrel?

Post Office Bay is a Floreana attraction, but it **is not specified as a mandatory stop** on this particular excursion. Confirm the exact route before traveling.

## Bartolomé Island: Pinnacle Rock, volcanic trails and snorkeling

Bartolomé is a small volcanic island in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), known for its viewpoint above the bay and **Pinnacle Rock**. It offers one of Ecuador's most recognizable island panoramas: dark volcanic slopes, sandy beaches, green-blue waters and a slender rock formation rising near the shore.

The Ada Tours boat excursion includes a walk up to the highest viewpoint, followed by time on the beach or for snorkeling. **The excursion lasts 6 hours.** This is a standalone island outing, not a cruise around the whole archipelago.

## Hiking to the Bartolomé viewpoint: what to expect

The walk up the volcanic slope takes **about 30 minutes**. Along the trail, layers of solidified volcanic material, dry terrain and the near absence of tall trees are clearly visible. The reward is a view of Pinnacle Rock, neighboring Santiago Island and the surrounding waters.

In good visibility, you can see **North Seymour, Baltra, Santa Cruz, Rábida and Chinese Hat Islet**. What can be seen in the distance depends on weather and clouds, so not every island will be distinguishable every day.

Although the ascent is fairly short, heat, sun and wind can make the exposed trail challenging. Wear stable footwear and bring water, a hat and UV protection. Travelers with reduced mobility should discuss whether the climb is suitable and whether there is an option to wait without ascending.

## Why visit Pinnacle Rock?

Pinnacle Rock is a volcanic formation that has become a symbol of Bartolomé. It is recognizable for its tall, narrow shape and location beside small beaches. The viewpoint brings the island's geology into focus: bays and volcanic deposits are visible together, against an almost vegetation-free landscape.

If your goal is **a panoramic photograph of the Galápagos**, Bartolomé differs from islands offering long walks through inhabited areas or wildlife viewing in mangrove lagoons. Here you can concentrate on the forms of the landscape and the geological origins of the archipelago.

## Beaches, penguins and underwater life

After the viewpoint walk, the itinerary provides time for **relaxing on the beach or snorkeling**. Galápagos penguins, sea turtles, rays, iguanas, sea lions and a variety of fish may be encountered near Bartolomé. Actual wildlife sightings depend on season, sea conditions and animal behavior.

Snorkeling involves swimming near the surface with a mask. **It is not the same as scuba diving.** We do not promise a diving instructor, tanks or a full scuba excursion. Before entering the water, the guide should confirm the permitted area, current conditions and suitability of the activity for the participants' abilities. Swimming is not permitted at every beach on the island.

For the marine part of the excursion, bring swimwear, a towel and dry clothes to change into: the itinerary specifically allows for changing before beach time.

## Guide, lunch and price

**The excursion costs $525.** It includes a transfer, lunch and the services of a guide speaking **English or Spanish**. A Russian-speaking guide is not specified for this product.

Additional activities, the separately listed **Galápagos National Park entrance fee ($200 per person)** and the **transit card ($20 per person)** are excluded from that amount. The park fee and card relate to visiting the archipelago as a whole: charging them again as a mandatory payment for each island excursion would be incorrect. The final amount depends on fees already paid on entry and the traveler's category.

Weather can affect the order of stops, disembarkation and whether snorkeling is possible. It is sensible to keep some flexibility in the island itinerary, particularly if a flight or another fixed connection follows the excursion.

## Bartolomé or Isabela: which excursion should you choose?

| Island | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Bartolomé | Pinnacle Rock panorama and beach time |
| Isabela | Lagoons, flamingos and Tintoreras |

For lagoons, mangrove vegetation and lively coastal channels, consider the [Isabela Island boat excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/isabela-island-speedboat-tour/). If you want to climb to a viewpoint, see Pinnacle Rock and, conditions permitting, snorkel, choose Bartolomé.

Both are among the [Galápagos Islands excursions](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/), but provide different experiences. You can also compare them with the more relaxed nature-focused [Santa Cruz Island excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/santa-cruz-island-tour/), which emphasizes land attractions and giant tortoises.

## Frequently asked questions about the Bartolomé excursion

### Is the climb to the viewpoint difficult?

The ascent takes approximately **30 minutes** on an exposed trail under the sun. Assess the suitable level of physical exertion in view of participants' health and mobility.

### Is snorkeling mandatory?

No. The itinerary offers time for beach relaxation or snorkeling, and swimming depends on conditions in the permitted area.

### Can you see Galápagos penguins?

The waters around Bartolomé are part of their habitat, but an encounter on any particular day is not guaranteed.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch, a transfer and an English- or Spanish-speaking guide are included.

### Do I need to pay the national park entrance fee again?

The fee is paid on entering the Galápagos according to the visitor category that applies. If it has already been paid for the current visit, the $200 amount should not be treated as another mandatory charge for each excursion.

## Tours including a boat excursion to Bartolomé Island

[Bartolomé Island](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) is one of the most recognizable destinations in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The viewpoint overlooks volcanic slopes, bays and the sharp outline of Pinnacle Rock. A notable feature of this island is the combination of a short uphill walk, beach time and the possibility of observing wildlife near the coast.

Here we have collected {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include the specific [Bartolomé boat excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/bartolome-island-boat-tour/) in their itineraries. When choosing a multi-day tour, distinguish the confirmed excursion day from other possible visits around the archipelago: not every Galápagos itinerary includes this island.

## Baltra, the volcanic trail and the Pinnacle Rock panorama

The boat itinerary is associated with [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) and Bartolomé. After arriving on the island, travelers climb to its highest viewpoint. Our itinerary allows around **30 minutes** for the ascent. The trail passes through dry volcanic terrain, and the view from above reveals Pinnacle Rock and neighboring islands.

There is then time on the beach and a chance to go snorkeling. The archipelago's coastal waters are home to sea lions, turtles, rays, fish and Galápagos penguins. Sightings of particular species always depend on natural conditions; naming these animals does not guarantee that each one will be seen.

Snorkeling and relaxing on the beach are alternative ways to spend the allocated time. Full scuba diving is a different type of excursion and requires a separate diving product.

## What the excursion includes and what costs extra

The standalone Bartolomé excursion lasts **6 hours** and costs **$525**. Services include an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, a transfer and lunch. Additional activities and mandatory Galápagos National Park fees are listed among the exclusions.

Travelers should distinguish the cost of the excursion from general fees for visiting the protected islands. The **national park entrance fee ($200 for the relevant visitor category)** and **transit card ($20)** are paid separately. The actual park rate depends on visitor category: the archipelago government's official resource lists different rates according to age, nationality and residency. Check the category that applies to you and the current payment rules before traveling.

These charges should not automatically be added to every excursion day again: paying general entry fees during a multi-day trip differs from pricing separate island outings. Check the complete terms of the journey in the relevant tour itinerary.

## Choosing a multi-day itinerary including Bartolomé

When comparing tours, check whether Bartolomé has its own day, whether a boat transfer is included and how many other islands travelers will visit. The Bartolomé excursion particularly suits people who want to see volcanic scenery, climb to the famous viewpoint and combine it with time at the beach.

If your main goal is to watch large colonies of seabirds on land, compare the [North Seymour excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/). Travelers wishing to scuba dive can choose a separate [two-dive day](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/galapagos-two-dive-day/). The difference lies in the activities and conditions, not simply in the names of islands visited.

When planning a multi-day journey, allow time for flights between mainland Ecuador and the islands, airport transfers, weather-related restrictions on sea crossings and national park requirements. Confirm that the excursion is actually included in the tour you select.

## Frequently asked questions about tours including Bartolomé

### How long does the boat excursion last?

The excursion takes **6 hours**, with approximately 30 minutes of that day allotted to climbing to the viewpoint.

### What language does the guide speak?

English and Spanish are confirmed for this excursion. A Russian-speaking guide is not automatically included in the price.

### Does the $525 include entry to Galápagos National Park?

No. The national park fee and transit card are charged separately. Their amounts and payment arrangements depend on the rules and the visitor category.

### How does Bartolomé differ from North Seymour?

The highlight of [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) is the volcanic panorama of Pinnacle Rock, with a climb and time on the beach. [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) is especially interesting for watching frigatebirds, boobies and other birds on land.

## Floreana Island from Santa Cruz: Galápagos wildlife and early settlers' history

[Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) is one of the most unusual islands in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Its natural attractions are intertwined with the history of mariners, whalers, pirates and settlers. For travelers, it is an opportunity to discover another side of the Galápagos after visiting the more populated Santa Cruz.

Our excursion departs from [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/) on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and continues to Floreana. The duration is **6 hours** and the price is **$366**. A transfer, lunch and the services of an English- or Spanish-speaking guide are included.

## Why Floreana is known far beyond the archipelago

Floreana's history is connected to Pacific sea routes. Sailors and whalers passing through used the island during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. At Post Office Bay, a remarkable system developed for forwarding letters: travelers left messages and other ships carried them along their routes.

Later, the island became one of the archipelago's earliest permanently inhabited places. Stories about early settlers include harsh living conditions, water shortages and dramatic events of the 1930s. Galápagos Conservancy highlights Floreana for its complicated human history and rare combination of isolated nature and traces of early settlement.

**The Ada Tours excursion introduces the general history of Floreana**, but does not explicitly guarantee a visit to the particular postal barrel, caves or history museums. Treat these as background to the destination, not promised stops.

## Volcanic shores and marine life

The island is bordered by volcanic shorelines and small coastal areas with a variety of marine animals. Travelers may see **blue-footed boobies, sea turtles and whitetip reef sharks** during the visit. These are wild animals in their natural habitat, so sightings of a particular species cannot be guaranteed on a particular day.

Floreana's marine landscape differs from the highland land-based itinerary on Santa Cruz. Coastal scenery, birds and ocean wildlife take center stage here. Sightings depend on weather, sea conditions and the route.

Do not assume that scuba diving, snorkeling or every well-known natural site on the island is included: these activities are not confirmed as part of this excursion.

## How the excursion from Puerto Ayora is organized

The confirmed itinerary links Puerto Ayora, Santa Cruz and Floreana. For an inter-island journey, checking transport and weather restrictions in advance is especially important: sea conditions can affect travel time and the ability to disembark. The type of vessel and detailed schedule are arranged separately.

**The $366 price** applies to this excursion product. It includes an English- or Spanish-speaking guide, a transfer and lunch. The **Galápagos National Park entrance fee ($200 per person)**, **transit card ($20 per person)**, medical insurance and personal expenses are paid separately.

Ada Tours may change the order of attractions when necessary. This matters on island itineraries, where weather and sea conditions can affect plans even with a favorable forecast.

## Floreana or Santa Cruz: which should you choose?

| Excursion | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Floreana | Marine nature and settlers' history |
| Santa Cruz | Giant tortoises and lava tunnels |

If you want to see tortoises in the green highlands and walk through underground volcanic tunnels, start with the [Santa Cruz excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/santa-cruz-island-tour/). If you are more interested in coastal fauna, marine scenery and the history of settlement, choose Floreana.

During your trip, observe conservation rules: do not feed animals, leave authorized trails, collect natural objects or approach birds for photographs. You can also compare island itineraries in the [Ecuador tours catalog](/ecuador/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Floreana trip

### How much does the Floreana excursion cost?

The Ada Tours listing gives **$366**. Park fees, the transit card, medical insurance and personal expenses are listed separately.

### Where does the excursion start?

The stated departure point is **Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz Island**. The program lasts 6 hours.

### Can you guarantee a sea turtle sighting?

No. The species named in the itinerary occur naturally in the archipelago, but specific encounters depend on timing, weather and animal behavior.

## Diving in the Galápagos: a day with 2 dives

The waters of the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are home to sea turtles, rays, sea lions and several species of shark. However, diving around different islands requires different levels of preparation: there are relatively calm reef sites as well as strong-current locations suited to experienced divers.

Our excursion includes **2 dives in one day, a check dive, an English-speaking naturalist guide or divemaster, standard equipment, a snack and lunch**. This is a group activity. The particular dive site depends on the operating schedule and national park rules; a list of possible sites does not mean all of them will be visited on the same day.

## Two schedules: nearby and distant dive sites

Pickup from the hotel is scheduled for **08:00**. The rest of the day depends on how far away the dive site is. For a nearby site, the check dive is scheduled for 09:30, the first dive for 10:30, the second for 12:45 and return to the dive center for around 15:15. At a more distant site, the corresponding stages begin about one hour later, with return planned by 16:30.

The first dive is planned for **18–25 m** and up to one hour, and the second for **18–20 m** and also up to one hour. A surface interval of approximately **1.5 hours** is provided between them. These are the planning parameters of our excursion; actual dive profiles, depths and time underwater must reflect each participant's level, weather, currents and the divemaster's decision.

The excursion uses the dive boat **L/P El Galapago I**, equipped with navigation and communication systems and onboard oxygen. Check the vessel and group arrangements for the confirmed departure, as marine excursion schedules can change.

## Where the dives may take place

Each site has its own underwater landscape. The possible locations include:

- [Bartolomé](/ecuador/place/bartolome-island/) and [Cousins Rock](/ecuador/place/cousins-rock/): reefs and underwater walls, with chances to see turtles, rays and reef fish.
- [Gordon Rocks](/ecuador/place/gordon-rocks/): a rocky dive site with strong currents, known for hammerhead shark sightings. This option is intended for experienced divers.
- [Mosquera Islet](/ecuador/place/mosquera-islet/) and the channel near [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/): sandy and rocky areas with sharks, sea lions, fish and rays.
- [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/): reef areas near Punta Cormorant, Champion and Enderby, with possible turtle and sea lion sightings.

Daphne, Plazas, Santa Fe and Cape Carrión are also named in the program. **These are alternative dive sites, not one combined route.** The destination depends on the weekday, park permits, weather and the operator's decision. Encounters with individual animal species are likewise not guaranteed.

## Diver qualifications and special conditions at Gordon Rocks

Participation in the standard program requires a **PADI, NAUI, CMAS or equivalent certification**; the minimum age for this excursion is **12 years**. Certified beginners may be eligible for most of the listed sites, but the dive team makes the final decision based on actual conditions.

**Gordon Rocks has additional requirements.** The conditions mention 25 logged dives and an assessment by the dive guide; more detailed wording specifies 25 dives within the preceding 18 months and a skills check. Access to this site is therefore confirmed individually by the dive center. Holding a basic entry-level certificate alone does not guarantee eligibility for Gordon Rocks.

If a participant reports a medical condition, or belongs to the program's age category over 60 without recent diving experience, a medical certificate may be required. Detailed medical restrictions and fitness to dive must be discussed with the dive center before heading out to sea.

## Equipment and safety after diving

Standard equipment is provided for the day, but some items in the complete program carry separate charges: a DIN adapter, nitrox and a dive computer. **Do not assume every optional extra is included** in the excursion price. Hotel accommodation and other days of a multi-day tour are also outside the services of a single dive day.

After **2 dives**, the timing of your return flight is particularly important. Divers Alert Network recommends at least **18 hours before flying after repetitive no-decompression dives**, with longer intervals reducing risk further. This is general safety guidance, not personal medical clearance: for complex dive profiles, symptoms or other risk factors, the interval may need to be longer. Agree the plan with a professional divemaster and, if necessary, a diving-medicine physician.

Diving in the Galápagos takes place at authorized marine sites in accordance with conservation rules. Do not feed, chase or touch animals. A separate [4–5-day Ada Tours itinerary for divers](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) lets travelers include diving within a longer island stay.

## Frequently asked questions about diving in the Galápagos

### How many dives are included in one day?

**Two**, with a surface interval between them, plus a snack and lunch. Exact timings depend on the distance to the selected dive site.

### Can beginners dive at Gordon Rocks?

Do not count on this site without documented experience. Gordon Rocks has additional requirements concerning the number of dives and a skills assessment.

### Will we dive at Bartolomé and Floreana on the same day?

That is not promised. Bartolomé, Floreana and the other sites are alternatives in the schedule; 2 dives are carried out on the approved daily route.

### How soon can I fly after two dives?

For repetitive no-decompression dives, DAN recommends at least 18 hours at the surface before flying. The individual plan must account for the dive profile and the diver's health.
